LESSON: WATER

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: RESOURCES IN OUR ENVIRONMENT Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugges
Topic 3.1: Water
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Water, part of RESOURCES IN OUR ENVIRONMENT Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugges in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we store water?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Water together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: Teamwork as learners walk around the neighbourhood to identify different ways of

storing water in groups.

Values:
● Social justice: Cooperation as learners walk around the neighbourhood to establish different ways of storing water.

● Responsibility: Hard work skills as learners store water appropriately at home and school.

59

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health promotion issues: Preventive health as learners store water appropriately at home and school to prevent

communicable diseases.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Creative Arts Activities: Drawing different Forms as learners use different items used to store water.

Suggested Learning Resources:
